headline_finding.claim: On an agent-capable adapter, review cost scales with repo surface rather than diff size.
headline_finding.evidence: senior_code_review 268,296 cached input for a 20-line diff at $1.038807 (6.5x the writing phase); security_review 288,292 cached. Both reviews 59% of run cost vs 9% for both writing passes. Same shape previously observed on antigravity-worker (flash-agsdk leg); claude-cli is a different adapter.
headline_finding.counterweight: That cost bought the quality: all four senior-review defects (F1, F2, S1, S2) required reading beyond the diff. S1/S2 required grepping the whole apps/docs tree; F2 required opening toggleLabelGroup, a function the diff never touched.
headline_finding.transfers_to: policies and adapters not exercised in either comparison
headline_finding.why_it_transfers: Two adapters with different vendor paths, different auth, and different model families converge on the same structural property. That is worth more than any cost number in either comparison, because it is the one finding that generalises beyond the policies actually run.
headline_finding.misreading_warning: Anyone who reads "59% of cost went to review" without "and that is what found the four defects" will draw the wrong conclusion and start trimming review scope. The counterweight is not optional context: all four defects required reading past the diff, and F2 required opening toggleLabelGroup, a function the diff never touches.

methodology_finding.claim: The legs that received no pre-solved trap answers are the legs whose results are usable.
methodology_finding.detail: This run was the second of four legs to receive no pre-solved trap answers. Both withheld-help legs (flash-agsdk-only and opus-plus-sonnet-max) derived every trap discrimination unaided. The two legs that received help (opus-plus-flash-v37, opus-only-v5) are the two whose results are confounded; opus-only says so in its own report.
methodology_finding.scope: a finding about how to run comparisons, not about which policy is better
